The problem is caused by saving too much state in `onSaveInstanceState`. For details see [here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/44738411/5635880). Where is all the saved state coming from? Is it being saved by the views? You can use something like [TooLargeTool](https://github.com/guardian/toolargetool) to debug this. If it's being saved the Activities or Fragments you can use [Bridge](https://github.com/livefront/bridge) to get around it. If it's all in the views themselves, that's a bit trickier. (`Bridge` doesn't currently support saving state for views, but we're looking into it.)
@byencho, which state are you referring to? Do you mean internal Android view/app state or react state stored in components?

@dluksza I'm not sure what the specific state it _is_, but the point of entry into the OS (via an `onSaveInstanceState` method) is either an Activity / Fragment or a View. I'd doubt that the data saved by basic Views internally on their own would cause the problem so I'd think that somewhere the library is manually saving some state in one of these places. I don't know enough about the library itself to say more than that at the moment.

Unfortunately
```bash
$ grep -r onSaveInstanceState node_modules
```
returns no results. I'm also not saving state manually in android app. Maybe it is done by third party library that is transitive dependency of one of `react-native` libs...

@dluksza Interesting. OK then I'd recommend taking a look at using [TooLargeTool](https://github.com/guardian/toolargetool) to try and debug what's going on to see if anything being saved jumps out at you as being unusually large. You can see if there are any custom key / value pairs in the bundles or if its only Android OS related. A typical Activity should have a Bundle with the keys `android:support:fragment`, `android:fragments`, `android:viewHierarchyState`. Anything else would point to some custom data being saved _somewhere_. Or if the `android:support:fragment` / `android:viewHierarchyState` values are large you could investigate in the Fragments / Views for more details.

It's certainly possible there is just too much vanilla view state being saved. That would require either (a) a very large number of views that save a decent amount of state (like an `EditText`) or (b) a small number of views that are saving an abnormally large amount of state based on user input (again like an `EditText`). I've actually tested this before : if you copy about 14 chapters of Moby Dick into an `EditText` you can trigger this crash. (That seems to be the type of scenario causing problems [here](https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/WordPress-Android/issues/5456).)
